newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Generator blow up starts fire at Bahrain hotel.
newsitem.headline: Generator blow up starts fire at Bahrain hotel.

text.p: A power generator blew up at a luxury hotel in the Bahraini capital Manama on Saturday, causing a fire, a government official said.
"The fire at the Diplomat Hotel was caused by an electricity generator explosion," the official said. "The blaze occured on the 14th floor, but there were no casualties or damage."
One firefighter at the 14-storey hotel said: "The fire was small but the smoke was thick." Three people were wounded in a blast which rocked the same five-star hotel in February 1996.
Residents and local newspapers said a fire had damaged Moonlight Restaurant near Ramada Hotel in Manama on Friday night, but there was no immediate report of casualties.

Another blaze on Friday gutted a sweet factory and damaged a nearby building and several residential rooms occupied by Asian workers in Muharraq, linked to Manama by a three km (two mile) causeway. A third fire destroyed a building also in Muharraq, they said.
It was not immediately clear what caused the Friday fires.

Last Tuesday an explosion rocked a hotel in central Manama and witnesses said part of the roof of the hotel's nightclub had collapsed. A government spokesman said initial reports indicated that a gas leak appeared to have been the cause.
A series of arson attacks in early June were described by a government official as "continued acts of terrorism."

Members of the island's majority Moslem Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press the Sunni-led governemnt to introduce economic and political reforms.
